# Aaron Wetzler

Academic homepage for Aaron Wetzler, CTO of an early-stage company building toward a future enabled by Physical AI. Previously Incubation and ML Lead at Apple and CTO of Camerai (acquired). Research areas include computer vision, machine learning, gesture recognition, and numerical geometry.

The homepage has 19 publications, 23 student projects, two theses, six research videos and nine patent lines. It consolidates the academic content previously split between the homepage and archive. Publications include conference and workshop papers, journal articles, a book chapter and a preprint. Mobile Point Fusion and Freehand Voxel Carving Scanning on a Mobile Device are student projects, not publications; their source links and citations remain available. The ECCV Beam/prism demonstration remains in Publications. Sixteen publications and two projects have BibTeX files.

Learning Invariant Representations of Planar Curves is listed as ICLR 2017 (preprint 2016), with its OpenReview link. The 2026 NeurIPS Robot Learning Workshop paper on robot-free demonstrations and the 2020 CoBe paper on coded beacons are retained. Conference and preprint versions are combined. Source links, publication PDFs where available, BibTeX files, posters, slides, videos, patent records and dataset links are listed directly on the homepage and in `data/site-content.json`.

All publication and project thumbnail frames use the same 184-by-115-pixel rectangular format. CoBe uses its original car photograph without the black frame; Deep Stereo uses two matched original source panels with equal horizontal alignment. Other selected figures use display-only CSS fitting, with a brightness adjustment for the mobile voxel illustration. Machine-readable records include source provenance, figure references and both stereo image panels. The NeurIPS workshop entry links directly to `https://openreview.net/forum?id=czwjjI5kkm` and its PDF. Its thumbnail is Aaron's supplied wearable-glove and matched-robot-hand figure at `assets/publications/neurips-robot-free-demonstrations.jpg`, preserved unchanged and displayed in full without cropping.

All 23 student projects have independent public GitHub repositories, linked from the homepage and STUDENT_PROJECTS.md. Fifteen include recovered historical source or pinned original upstream code. GrayOwl retains project information and public links; its source code and updated notebook have been withdrawn. CutOut includes original Android Java/JNI C++ source recovered from Elad Richardson on 2026-11-13; its historical Eclipse interface remains unbuilt. The separately updated recovered C++/OpenCV operators now have Android and iOS interfaces, a local drawing interface and a native CLI with recorded macOS and Linux checks. Its separate related prototype still has unverified authorship. Smartphone Game additionally links Idan Banani’s source repository without importing it or verifying a build. Three have documents without verified app source, and three have introductory READMEs. The JSON records expose repository, source_status, resources and upstream revisions where applicable. Do not interpret a repository link as proof of available or runnable code. Original source/setup notes and missing dependencies are documented in each README; complete modern application builds are not implied. Existing third-party terms and student attribution are retained, with no blanket relicensing.

The current multi-view iPhone presentation removes one database screenshot containing application login details from slide 7; historical Git copies retain the original. QRoom's archived PHP backend has confirmed security vulnerabilities and must not be deployed. Pinned upstream source needs separate credential and vendor-license review before reuse.

The PhD thesis is Topics in Computational Geometric Vision, by Aaron Wetzler, submitted to the Technion in August 2017 under Prof. Ron Kimmel's supervision. The full original 151-page PDF is hosted directly on the website. The undergraduate thesis is Low Cost 3D Laser Scanning Unit with Application to Face Recognition, University of Cape Town, 2005. Both are separate from Publications.

HandNet is publicly available without a gate on Hugging Face. The complete release contains 214,971 original frames (202,198 train, 10,000 test, 2,773 validation) and seven unchanged distribution archives, totaling 25,475,576,842 bytes. Transformed variants reuse original examples. The data is licensed under CC BY 4.0, permitting academic and commercial reuse with attribution, a license link and an indication of changes. Credit Aaron Wetzler, Ron Slossberg and Ron Kimmel and cite their BMVC 2015 paper. The historical MATLAB repository retains its separate original terms.

The HandNet project page embeds a self-contained 20-sample viewer served by this GitHub Pages repository. Its scripts, vendored dependencies and sample assets use relative URLs; it does not depend on a Hugging Face iframe or CDN. The separate Hugging Face research Space and Parquet preview contain 96 derived visualization rows, not the full dataset. Display images and calibrated point clouds illustrate measured annotations; they do not constitute learned detector inference or a full anatomical hand-joint skeleton.

The HandNet page also retains the paper, poster, presentation, supplementary archive and citation links. The homepage includes all 21 former archive student projects and all six demonstration video links. archive.html is now only a compatibility redirect; old Publications, Projects, Theses and Videos anchors resolve to the corresponding homepage sections, with direct section links available without JavaScript. The homepage and HandNet project page share typography, navigation and theme. No visitor analytics or tracking script is installed.

The second recovery pass adds Mobile Point Fusion v2.3 (January 2015 snapshot), the original stereo_vision repository pinned at 69a76767b2ce74f7b580ddb7b81a43fbb1dd346b, three Face Depth MATLAB fragments and a related CutOut prototype. GrayOwl source code and updated geometry work were subsequently withdrawn and are no longer linked. New imports use source/original/. Raw mail, credentials and unreviewed archives stay private. Separately labeled updated/ components, where present, preserve the historical snapshots and document their own tests and scope.

Code & Data links all 12 public software/data repositories, including the Beltrami implementations and Blender Neural Composer, with historical tools and forks identified as such. The student-project directory remains separate.

Android 3D Scanner credits students Arkadi Godlin and Alex Kligman and separately identifies lab engineer Alon Zvirin, correcting the historical spelling Alon Zivrin while retaining it in metadata.

Four separately labeled updated Python components previously recorded 70 passing unit tests and executed Jupyter notebooks on macOS/Python 3.14 (not rerun after 2026-11-12): HeartBeat signal processing (20), Volume Carving geometry/occupancy (16), Face Depth difference features (18), and CutOut Fast Marching (16). Each project row links its notebook and Colab. These are scoped demonstrations, not restored complete mobile/vision/flight applications. Original-source availability and updated-component validation are separate fields in the machine-readable index.

Author-supplied resources added on 2026-11-13: Smartphone Game source at https://github.com/IdanBanani/iOS-4-2D-game-for-iPad (inspected commit 270b45ce6a1e149209e1d595e492766ede3b7747; application build unverified); CamPong poster, presentation with embedded historical recording and project overview under https://github.com/twerdster/campong/tree/main/original, plus https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=msWkridhFyQ and Nofar Carmeli’s preferred website https://nofar.carme.li/; RiftFusion’s original presentation at https://github.com/twerdster/oculus-positional-tracking/blob/main/original/RiftFusion-Presentation.pptx and author-supplied profile links. CamPong and RiftFusion application source remains unavailable. Private correspondence and shared-folder access keys are not published.

CutOut Android source recovery, 2026-11-13: https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/tree/main/source/original/android-app contains author-supplied historical Java/JNI C++ source, resources and build metadata. Source/build notes are at https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/docs/original-android.md. The three-file related prototype remains separately linked at https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/tree/main/source/original/related-prototype with unverified authorship. Missing historical dependencies and the unbuilt Eclipse interface remain explicit; the later updated implementation has its own execution records. The separately written Python Fast Marching exercise retains its recorded 16 component tests; those do not validate the historical Android interface. Elad Richardson’s permission to host recovered project code is his permission only and does not speak for other contributors. Recovery and that permission do not establish a new software license or manuscript approval.

CutOut platform guides: native CLI https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/native/README.md; local drawing interface https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/desktop/README.md; Android https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/android/README.md; iOS https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/ios/README.md. Updated interfaces share recovered Lab FIGTree/histogram density, pixel-grid Dijkstra or MegaWave FLST/tree Dijkstra, and optional alpha-refinement operators. Native validation records: macOS https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/validation/VALIDATION.json and Ubuntu Linux https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/validation/LINUX_VALIDATION.json. The Linux record contains 31 named ASan/UBSan checks, repeated with unsigned char, 25 CLI cases (15 successful including eight photograph operator combinations, 10 expected errors) and six isolated original-body comparisons. Sanitizers cover the port and bundled ANN/FIGTree/MegaWave; external OpenCV 4.6.0 and system libraries are not instrumented, and leak checking is not claimed. These Linux results cover the native CLI, not the desktop drawing interface. Android https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/android/VALIDATION.json separates an Android 14 emulator and one Pixel 2/Android 10 physical-device run, with 14-case fixture sets and separately scoped touch, gallery, error and persistence checks. The iOS fixture record https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/ios/VALIDATION.json describes 14 scripted physical-device segmentation calls; the UI-test runner builds but its recorded attempt stopped at automation initialization before any test case started. Fixture calls and layout inspection do not establish touch/picker/share coverage, simulator support or minimum-version compatibility. The coffee photograph has no independent reference mask. The recorded runs do not establish photographic accuracy, bitwise equivalence across devices or equivalence to the historical APK. Original 319 Android files, three related prototype files and earlier 16-test Python metadata remain separate; source-bearing repository count stays 15.

Hand tracking: Sa'ar Zehavi supplied unfinished April 2013 design slides on 2026-11-13, preserved at https://github.com/twerdster/hand-tracking-pmd/blob/main/docs/real-time-hand-tracking-draft-2013.pptx. The slides retain placeholders and a first-order approximation step he said he had already removed. They are historical draft material, not a final implementation or new execution evidence. The existing nine recovered source files and June report are unchanged; no additional code arrived in the attachment. The contribution adds no standard reuse license, and embedded third-party illustrations retain their original rights. See https://github.com/twerdster/hand-tracking-pmd/blob/main/PROVENANCE.md. Vlad Ostrovski's later reply confirms RiftFusion's already-linked historical video; no duplicate resource or new application source is added.
